SFixture: John 5, in the words of the WEB
Pm
V1
TAfter these things, there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
V2
TNow in Jerusalem by the sheep gate, there is a pool, which is called in Hebrew, “Bethesda”, having five porches.
V3
TIn these lay a great multitude of those who were sick, blind, lame, or paralyzed, waiting for the moving of the water;
V4
Tfor an angel went down at certain times into the pool and stirred up the water. Whoever stepped in first after the stirring of the water was healed of whatever disease he had.
V5
TA certain man was there who had been sick for thirty-eight years.
V6
TWhen Jesus saw him lying there, and knew that he had been sick for a long time, he asked him,
W “Do you want to be made well?”
Pm
V7
TThe sick man answered him, “Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up, but while I’m coming, another steps down before me.”
Pm
V8
TJesus said to him,
W “Arise, take up your mat, and walk.”
Pm
V9
TImmediately, the man was made well, and took up his mat and walked.
Pm
V10
TSo the Jews said to him who was cured, “It is the Sabbath. It is not lawful for you to carry the mat.”
Pm
V11
THe answered them, “He who made me well said to me,
W ‘Take up your mat and walk.’
T ”
Pm
V12
TThen they asked him, “Who is the man who said to you,
W ‘Take up your mat and walk’
T?”
Pm
V13
TBut he who was healed didn’t know who it was, for Jesus had withdrawn, a crowd being in the place.
Pm
V14
TAfterward Jesus found him in the temple and said to him,
W “Behold, you are made well. Sin no more, so that nothing worse happens to you.”
Pm
V15
TThe man went away, and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well.
V16
TFor this cause the Jews persecuted Jesus and sought to kill him, because he did these things on the Sabbath.
V17
TBut Jesus answered them,
W “My Father is still working, so I am working, too.”
Pm
V18
TFor this cause therefore the Jews sought all the more to kill him, because he not only broke the Sabbath, but also called God his own Father, making himself equal with God.
V19
TJesus therefore answered them,
W “Most certainly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing of himself, but what he sees the Father doing. For whatever things he does, these the Son also does likewise.
V20
WFor the Father has affection for the Son, and shows him all things that he himself does. He will show him greater works than these, that you may marvel.
V21
WFor as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, even so the Son also gives life to whom he desires.
V22
WFor the Father judges no one, but he has given all judgment to the Son,
V23
Wthat all may honor the Son, even as they honor the Father. He who doesn’t honor the Son doesn’t honor the Father who sent him.
Pm
V24
W“Most certainly I tell you, he who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and doesn’t come into judgment, but has passed out of death into life.
V25
WMost certainly I tell you, the hour comes, and now is, when the dead will hear the Son of God’s voice; and those who hear will live.
V26
WFor as the Father has life in himself, even so he gave to the Son also to have life in himself.
V27
WHe also gave him authority to execute judgment, because he is a son of man.
V28
WDon’t marvel at this, for the hour comes in which all who are in the tombs will hear his voice
V29
Wand will come out; those who have done good, to the resurrection of life; and those who have done evil, to the resurrection of judgment.
V30
WI can of myself do nothing. As I hear, I judge; and my judgment is righteous, because I don’t seek my own will, but the will of my Father who sent me.
Pm
V31
W“If I testify about myself, my witness is not valid.
V32
WIt is another who testifies about me. I know that the testimony which he testifies about me is true.
V33
WYou have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.
V34
WBut the testimony which I receive is not from man. However, I say these things that you may be saved.
V35
WHe was the burning and shining lamp, and you were willing to rejoice for a while in his light.
V36
WBut the testimony which I have is greater than that of John; for the works which the Father gave me to accomplish, the very works that I do, testify about me, that the Father has sent me.
V37
WThe Father himself, who sent me, has testified about me. You have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his form.
V38
WYou don’t have his word living in you, because you don’t believe him whom he sent.
Pm
V39
W“You search the Scriptures, because you think that in them you have eternal life; and these are they which testify about me.
V40
WYet you will not come to me, that you may have life.
V41
WI don’t receive glory from men.
V42
WBut I know you, that you don’t have God’s love in yourselves.
V43
WI have come in my Father’s name, and you don’t receive me. If another comes in his own name, you will receive him.
V44
WHow can you believe, who receive glory from one another, and you don’t seek the glory that comes from the only God?
Pm
V45
W“Don’t think that I will accuse you to the Father. There is one who accuses you, even Moses, on whom you have set your hope.
V46
WFor if you believed Moses, you would believe me; for he wrote about me.
V47
WBut if you don’t believe his writings, how will you believe my words?”
